character: Mel: everyday Kiwi woman, late 30s, the owner in this skit (fictional, as is Jono the sparky; the video carries an 'A skit · names made up' chip from frame 0). Dry and amused at the thumbs-up, never at Jono or herself; reads the 'contract' like a bored clerk reading out a very short will. General NZ accent, never a caricature, no announcer lift, no exclamation marks. Product lines are second-person or neutral tips ('Paste the thread…', 'That bit's on you'), never 'I use it' or a result claim, so an AI voice can never read as a customer testimonial.

Heat-pump wiring in that?' / Jono's 👍 / 'Sweet as, see you Monday'); the 👍 pulses (0.08–0.40), then the camera dives into it until it fills the frame (0.42–1.30), gavel squash 1.30

lines.delivery: Clerk reading the terms aloud, totally straight. Tiny beat after 'Clause one', 'thumbs up' dead level. Out by 3.16, before clause 2 pops (3.20).

lines.on_screen: 'CLAUSE 2 · Heat-pump wiring included?' + thumb slam (3.50); red marker '(unclear)' 3.70–4.00
lines.delivery: Same read, shorter: she has already stopped saying 'clause'. Out by 4.14.
Lowest and flattest of the three. Out by 5.17, so the dotted signature line (5.20–5.54) draws in silence.
The dry turn. 'Agreed' on its own with a full stop, then 'just never signed' a shade quieter, like admitting something small. Out by 6.97, before the whip to the laptop (7.06).

lines.delivery: A practical tip to a mate, not a pitch. Even pace; 'Q-S-me' clear (kyoo-ess-mee), never 'kiss me'. Out by 9.25.

lines.on_screen: Whip to the real live capture, qsme.co.nz Knowledge Hub (Agreements guide), held 12.32–15.94: 'AI never makes up an amount, a date or a name. Anything it was not given stays a [blank] for you.' Green underline 12.74–13.62, amber under '[blank]' 14.34–14.64

lines.text_v3: No made-up money. No made-up dates.

casting_line: Clause one: thumbs up. Two: thumbs up. Three: thumbs up. Agreed. Just never signed.
